Capability Coverage Test The model is complete when: every KF-2002 practice maps to at least one principal capability; every mandatory KF-2002 artefact has a capability responsible for its creation or maintenance; every KF-3001 invariant is protected by at least one capability (demonstrated individually in Appendix A); every KF-3001 interaction constraint is enforceable through the capabilities in Appendix B; every capability has an upstream derivation; every capability has at least one independently observable conformance condition; no capability exists solely because a familiar technology category suggests it; and no upstream obligation remains unsupported. Part IX · Capability Conformance 12. Capability Conformance A capability is conformant when an implementation demonstrates that all required behaviours are realised; all principal information objects can be produced, maintained and retrieved; relationships are satisfied; protected invariants remain true whenever their scope applies; failure and indeterminate conditions are visible; the stated conformance condition can be demonstrated; and no prohibited substitution is used to claim satisfaction. Capability conformance may be assessed individually for diagnostic purposes, but architectural conformance is systemic . A capability cannot be declared conformant where an unsatisfied prerequisite or collaborating capability prevents its required behaviours or protected invariants from being realised. Conformance is not a component-by-component certification. 13. Capability Evidence Evidence may include representative end-to-end lifecycle cases; information-object inspection; invariant tests; prohibited-path tests; authority and permission checks; historical reconstruction; dependency-impact tests; degraded-state tests; cross-service reconciliation; and independent assurance results. Technology features or vendor claims are not, by themselves, evidence of capability conformance. 14. Capability Conformance and Capability Maturity Capability conformance is not the same as capability maturity, and the two are assessed separately. A conforming capability may exhibit different degrees of automation, scale, latency, usability, coverage, reliability, modality support and assurance independence. A manually maintained stewardship register may conform to C-CAP-02 while being operationally immature; a sophisticated AI governance platform may be non-conforming if it silently passes indeterminate evidence or collapses acceptance into model confidence. Maturity does not compensate for an absent required behaviour or a violated invariant. Part XI · Relationship to Subsequent Documents KF-3003 defines the logical services that expose and coordinate these capabilities; a service may realise several capabilities and a capability may be distributed across several services, and it will carry the typed relationships of §4 and §7 into service collaboration, constraint and evidence contracts. KF-3005 defines the lifecycle controls and gate logic through which the capabilities operate safely, including the transactional binding of gate decision and transition in C-CAP-08. KF-3008 assigns the authority and accountability of the participants exercising these capabilities (technical permission is assigned by SVC-16). KF-3007 defines the tests and evidence by which capability conformance is demonstrated, including the operating-criticality consequences of unavailability. KF-3009 preserves traceability from Canonical Principle through practice, invariant, capability, service, record, control and implementation. Closing Statement The Capability Model defines the complete set of abilities that a governed knowledge architecture must possess. It does not prescribe how those abilities are implemented. It ensures that, whatever form an implementation takes, it can identify and structure knowledge objects, establish and preserve their warrant, govern authority, versioning, release and change, control operational use, learn from outcomes, and demonstrate that these obligations remain satisfied over time.

d: The Logical Services Through Which Capabilities Are Exposed and Governed
x: Purpose KF-3002 defines what a governed knowledge architecture must be able to do. KF-3003 defines through which logical services those abilities are exposed, coordinated and governed — the execution architecture of the Knowledge Foundry. KF-3003 introduces no new obligations. It does not weaken an invariant, relax an interaction constraint, or select a technology. Its single question is: Through which logical services are the capabilities exposed, coordinated and governed, without violating any interaction constraint? A logical service is a stable responsibility exposed to authorised actors and other services through defined operations, information objects and controls. A service may later be realised by software, assigned human work, or a governed combination of both; KF-3003 fixes the responsibility, not the realisation. Relationship to Upstream Documents KF-3003 is bounded on three sides and may not exceed any of them. From KF-3002 , it inherits the twenty-four capabilities and their typed relationships. Every service realises one or more capabilities; no service exists without a capability basis. From KF-3001 , it inherits the twenty-two interaction constraints. Every constraint must be enforced at a defined service boundary; a service architecture that cannot enforce a constraint is non-conforming. From KF-3000 , it inherits the intent of the service catalogue. KF-3000 sketched a provisional service list and explicitly deferred the definitive catalogue to KF-3003 . This document establishes that definitive catalogue — nineteen logical services — and where it refines KF-3000 ’s provisional numbering, KF-3003 is authoritative and KF-3000 ’s §11–12 list and §22–24 crosswalks are read as pointing here. The direction of authority is strict: a service may choose how to expose a capability, but may never add to, weaken, or reinterpret the capability, invariant or constraint it inherits. The Distinctive Property — Interaction Governance A service architecture is not merely a decomposition of capabilities into components. Its distinctive and load-bearing property is interaction governance : it must guarantee that the interaction constraints IC-01–IC-22 hold in execution , not only on paper. Decomposition alone can satisfy every capability individually while allowing services to bypass one another — a version service that also releases, an application service that also accepts, an assurance service that authorises the transitions it audits. KF-3003 exists to make those bypasses structurally impossible by assigning each constraint to a boundary and each governed record to a single authoritative maintainer. Part VII is therefore the centre of this document, not an appendix to it. Service Admission Test A proposed logical service is admitted only where: it realises one or more KF-3002 capabilities; every capability it realises names it as the single accountable service, or names another service and this one as a supporting collaborator; it is the authoritative maintainer of a defined, non-overlapping set of information objects; its operations can be stated without naming a technology or product; it enforces, or participates in enforcing, at least one interaction constraint, or is required by a capability that does; it acquires no authority beyond the capabilities it realises; its conformance can be demonstrated independently. Design Principles for Service Definition SP-1 · Capability-derived services. Every service is justified by the capabilities it realises; none is admitted because a technology category suggests it. SP-2 · Single accountable service. Each capability has exactly one accountable service; other services may support it, but accountability is not shared. SP-3 · Authoritative information ownership. Each governed information object has exactly one authoritative-maintainer service; other services read it or request changes through a governed interaction. SP-4 · Constraint enforcement at a boundary. Every KF-3001 interaction constraint is enforced at a named service boundary, not left to convention. SP-5 · No authority accrual. Execution capacity confers no authority. A service that performs an operation does not thereby gain the right to authorise it. SP-6 · Coherent coarseness. Capabilities are grouped into one service only where they share information ownership and lifecycle role. Distinct governance obligations remain distinct services even where a single component might implement them. Version, acceptance and release are therefore three services, not one. SP-7 · Logical, not physical. Services are logical responsibilities. One may be distributed across components and several combined into one, provided their boundaries and authoritative ownership remain inspectable. SP-8 · Assurance independence. The conformance service is read-only with respect to the records it assesses and is never an operational prerequisite of the operations it audits. Service Specification Each service is specified through ten fields: Service statement , Purpose , Realised capabilities , Authoritative information objects , Service operations , Collaborations (typed: prerequisite, collaborating, constraining, evidence), Enforced interaction constraints , Authority boundary (what the service must not do), Operating criticality , and Conformance condition . Part I · Service Taxonomy 1. The Logical Services KF-3003 defines nineteen logical services, numbered sequentially and grouped by domain. Cross-cutting services are grouped together at the end of the sequence. Service Domain Accountable capabilities SVC-01 · Object Registry A A-CAP-01, A-CAP-03 SVC-02 · Representation A A-CAP-02 SVC-03 · Evidence B B-CAP-01 SVC-04 · Evaluation B B-CAP-02 SVC-05 · Justification B B-CAP-03, B-CAP-04 SVC-06 · Authority and Acceptance C C-CAP-01 SVC-07 · Stewardship and Review C C-CAP-02, C-CAP-03 SVC-08 · Lifecycle and Transition C C-CAP-08 SVC-09 · Version and Lineage C C-CAP-04, C-CAP-06 SVC-10 · Release C C-CAP-05 SVC-11 · Dependency C C-CAP-07 SVC-12 · Operationalisation D D-CAP-01 SVC-13 · Application and Outcome D D-CAP-02, D-CAP-03 SVC-14 · Retirement and Preservation D D-CAP-04 SVC-15 · Provenance and Traceability E E-CAP-01 SVC-16 · Access and Integrity E E-CAP-03 SVC-17 · Operating Condition and Exception E E-CAP-04 SVC-18 · Conformance and Audit E E-CAP-02 SVC-19 · Temporal Continuity E E-CAP-05 Every one of the twenty-four capabilities names exactly one accountable service (§5). The five Domain E services are cross-cutting: Provenance, Access, Operating Condition and Temporal Continuity constrain or supply evidence to the others, and Conformance reads all of them without altering any. Version, acceptance and release are three services. Version creation (SVC-09) is not acceptance (SVC-06) and neither is release (SVC-10). This three-way separation is the structural expression of IC-06, IC-08 and IC-09, and is the principal refinement of this document over the KF-3000 sketch. Part II · Domain A Services SVC-01 · Object Registry Service Service statement. Assigns and resolves durable object identity and routes intake to the responsible downstream service. Purpose. Establish identity as the single anchor of governance, distinct from version, representation and record identity. Realised capabilities. Accountable for A-CAP-01, A-CAP-03. Supports A-CAP-02. Authoritative information objects. Object Identity Record; Intake Record; Identity Resolution Decision; Resolution Result. Service operations. Register candidate; assign immutable identifier; resolve identifier to one object; assess intake relation to existing objects; retrieve current and historical governed context; expose unresolved identity conditions. Collaborations. Constrained by: SVC-16, SVC-17. Evidence from: SVC-15. Triggers: SVC-09 (version or lineage creation). Collaborates with: SVC-02, SVC-05, SVC-08 (context for resolution). Enforced interaction constraints. IC-05 (Identity Immutability). Authority boundary. Does not create versions, branches or consolidated successors; does not accept, release or retire; does not alter representation content. Operating criticality. Governance-critical; fail-closed — no progression without a resolved, unique identity. Conformance condition. Any registered object resolves to exactly one identity with recoverable origin and intake decision, and no identifier is reused. SVC-02 · Representation Service Service statement. Creates and maintains the inspectable representation of an object’s content, type and relationships. Purpose. Make objects inspectable so that evaluation, justification, governance and explanation can operate on explicit structure. Realised capabilities. Accountable for A-CAP-02. Supports A-CAP-03. Authoritative information objects. Structured Representation; Semantic Type Record; Metadata Record; Object Relationship Record; Representation Limitation Record. Service operations. Assign semantic type; represent constituent elements and relationships; attach metadata; link representation to object version; declare modality limitations. Collaborations. Prerequisite: SVC-01. Constrained by: SVC-16. Evidence from: SVC-15. Enforced interaction constraints. Participates in INV-02, INV-03 preservation; no primary IC boundary. Authority boundary. Does not evaluate, justify or accept; does not assign identity; does not conflate content with warrant. Operating criticality. Governance-critical — inspectability precedes all downstream governance. Conformance condition. For any representation, a reviewer can determine what it expresses, which object version it represents, how its elements relate and what modality limitations apply. Part III · Domain B Services SVC-03 · Evidence Service Service statement. Registers evidence and counter-evidence as governed records related to claims and objects. Purpose. Make evidential support, challenge and origin independently inspectable, distinct from the conclusions drawn from them. Realised capabilities. Accountable for B-CAP-01. Authoritative information objects. Evidence Record; Counter-Evidence Record; Evidence-to-Claim Link; Evidence Classification; Evidence Availability Status. Service operations. Register evidence; classify support, challenge or context; relate evidence to claims and objects; record availability; retain conflicting evidence. Collaborations. Prerequisite: SVC-01, SVC-02. Constrained by: SVC-16. Evidence from: SVC-15. Enforced interaction constraints. Participates in IC-20 (provenance of evidence). Authority boundary. Does not evaluate quality, construct justification or determine acceptance; does not delete counter-evidence. Operating criticality. Governance-critical — warrant depends on inspectable evidence. Conformance condition. For each material claim, the related evidence and counter-evidence, their origins, roles and availability are recoverable. SVC-04 · Evaluation Service Service statement. Assesses quality and fitness against explicit criteria and records the verdict. Purpose. Determine whether an object is suitable to proceed toward justification, distinct from establishing why it may be believed. Realised capabilities. Accountable for B-CAP-02. Authoritative information objects. Evaluation Criteria Record; Quality Assessment; Evaluation Verdict; Evaluation Exception; Confidence Record. Service operations. Apply criteria; assess quality, consistency, completeness and confidence; record pass, fail, return, pending or indeterminate; retain reasons; route incomplete assessments. Collaborations. Prerequisite: SVC-02, SVC-03. Constrained by: SVC-17. Evidence to: SVC-18. Enforced interaction constraints. Participates in INV-24 (no silent pass). Authority boundary. Does not construct justification or accept; does not define organisational thresholds. Operating criticality. Governance-critical — the quality gate precedes justification. Conformance condition. For any evaluation, the criteria, inputs, evaluator, result, confidence, reasons and disposition are recoverable. SVC-05 · Justification Service Service statement. Assembles and exposes inspectable warrant, and maintains epistemic status distinct from acceptance. Purpose. Establish why an object may be believed, and preserve uncertainty and dispute even where reliance is later permitted. Realised capabilities. Accountable for B-CAP-03, B-CAP-04. Authoritative information objects. Justification Record; Assumption Record; Rationale Record; Traceability Chain; Challenge Record; Epistemic Status Record; Confidence Record; Contestation Record; Epistemic Status Change Record. Service operations. Relate claims to evidence and counter-evidence; record assumptions and rationale; construct traceability; represent epistemic status; preserve prior epistemic states; expose warrant for independent inspection. Collaborations. Prerequisite: SVC-03, SVC-04. Collaborating: SVC-06 (justification–acceptance boundary). Constrained by: SVC-16. Evidence from: SVC-15. Enforced interaction constraints. IC-09 (Justification–Acceptance Separation), enforced jointly with SVC-06. Authority boundary. Does not accept, release or apply; does not let acceptance overwrite epistemic status; does not claim justification guarantees truth. Operating criticality. Governance-critical — justification is the warrant on which reliance rests. Conformance condition. An independent reviewer can reconstruct the reasons for and against belief, the assumptions, and the object’s epistemic standing separately from its acceptance state. Part IV · Domain C Services SVC-06 · Authority and Acceptance Service Service statement. Records the governed decision by which an identified authority permits reliance upon a justified object. Purpose. Separate epistemic warrant from institutional permission to rely. Realised capabilities. Accountable for C-CAP-01. Authoritative information objects. Acceptance Record; Refusal Record; Scope-of-Reliance Record; Authority Assignment Reference; Acceptance Condition Record. Service operations. Identify accepting authority; verify mandate, scope and effective period; record acceptance, provisional acceptance or refusal; define reliance scope and conditions; route refusals. Collaborations. Prerequisite: SVC-05, SVC-16. Collaborating: SVC-08. Triggers: SVC-10 (release), SVC-08 (transition). Evidence from: SVC-15. Enforced interaction constraints. IC-09 (with SVC-05); IC-13 (Authority Is Not Permission); IC-16 (Automated Authority Boundary). Authority boundary. Does not construct justification; does not create or release versions itself; does not assign permissions (that is SVC-16); does not become the final accountable authority where a human authority is required. Operating criticality. Governance-critical; fail-closed — no acceptance without an applicable authority. Conformance condition. Every accepted object carries a decision attributable to an authority whose mandate, scope and effective period applied, with reliance scope, conditions, date and supporting justification. SVC-07 · Stewardship and Review Service Service statement. Maintains ownership and accountability and determines whether standing governance conditions remain satisfied. Purpose. Preserve sustained human accountability and legitimacy across operational life. Realised capabilities. Accountable for C-CAP-02, C-CAP-03. Authoritative information objects. Stewardship Assignment; Responsibility Record; Stewardship History; Accountable Body Record; Review Schedule; Review Record; Compliance Assessment; Compliance Finding; Governance Exception. Service operations. Assign and transfer stewardship; schedule and record reviews; detect overdue reviews; evaluate compliance; raise triggers for suspension, evolution or retirement. Collaborations. Prerequisite: SVC-01. Collaborating: SVC-08. Constrained by: SVC-16, SVC-17. Triggers: SVC-08, SVC-09. Evidence from: SVC-15; Evidence to: SVC-18. Enforced interaction constraints. Participates in INV-10 (standing governance) upkeep; raises IC-03 suspension triggers. Authority boundary. Does not accept or release; does not execute the transitions it triggers (that is SVC-08); does not assign access permissions. Operating criticality. Governance-critical; recoverable within a defined period — a late review is bounded and must be visible as overdue. Conformance condition. Every operational object has a recoverable steward, review status and compliance standing, and no operational object is ownerless. SVC-08 · Lifecycle and Transition Service Service statement. Registers lifecycle events, evaluates gates and executes attributable state transitions as one governed operation. Purpose. Preserve controlled movement between lifecycle states and hold the sole right to change recorded state. Realised capabilities. Accountable for C-CAP-08. Authoritative information objects. Event Record; Gate Decision Record; Transition Record; Transition Warrant; Transition Status. Service operations. Register events; identify applicable gate; evaluate eligibility; bind gate decision and transition transactionally; attribute execution and authority separately; execute forward, return, suspension and retirement transitions. Collaborations. Collaborating: SVC-06, SVC-07, SVC-09, SVC-10, SVC-11, SVC-14. Constrained by: SVC-16, SVC-17. Evidence from: SVC-15, SVC-19; Evidence to: SVC-18. Enforced interaction constraints. IC-01 (Lifecycle State Authority); IC-02 (Gate Enforcement); IC-03 (Suspension Ownership). Authority boundary. Does not make the acceptance decision (that is SVC-06); does not define gate criteria (that is KF-3005 ); does not disposition dependencies (that is SVC-11). Only SVC-08 may alter recorded lifecycle state. Operating criticality. Governance-critical; fail-closed — an indeterminate or unavailable gate does not silently pass. Conformance condition. For every transition, the event, prior and proposed state, gate result, executor, accountable authority and outcome are recoverable under one transition identifier. SVC-09 · Version and Lineage Service Service statement. Creates immutable versions and preserves lineage across change, without altering enduring identity and without releasing anything. Purpose. Preserve every state of content and warrant as an immutable, recoverable version, and preserve predecessor–successor lineage — kept strictly distinct from acceptance and release. Realised capabilities. Accountable for C-CAP-04 (version), C-CAP-06 (evolution and lineage). Authoritative information objects. Version Record; Version State; Predecessor–Successor Link; Correction Record; Change Record; Lineage Record; Branch Record; Consolidation Record; Reactivation Proposal. Service operations. Create candidate and governed versions; preserve prior versions; prevent overwrite; identify predecessor and successor versions; branch, consolidate and supersede with explicit lineage; preserve correction history; route changed states for renewed warrant. Collaborations. Prerequisite: SVC-01, SVC-02. Collaborating: SVC-08, SVC-11. Constrained by: SVC-16. Evidence from: SVC-15; Evidence with: SVC-19. Enforced interaction constraints. IC-06 (Version Immutability); IC-07 (Branch and Consolidation Identity); IC-21 (Append-Only Correction, with SVC-19). Authority boundary. Does not accept, release or apply; does not create or mutate identity; version creation never implies release. A new version is never automatically released. Operating criticality. Governance-critical; fail-closed — no overwrite of a prior version. Conformance condition. For any object, its immutable versions, their order, correction and supersession relationships and full lineage are recoverable, distinct from whether any version is accepted or released. SVC-10 · Release Service Service statement. Designates an accepted version as eligible for a defined scope and period of operational reliance, and governs withdrawal and supersession of that eligibility. Purpose. Hold operational release as a distinct governed decision — separate from version creation and from acceptance — so that eligibility can be granted, retained, revalidated and withdrawn without touching version or identity. Realised capabilities. Accountable for C-CAP-05. Authoritative information objects. Release Record; Release Scope; Effective Period; Release Status; Withdrawal Record; Supersession Record; Revalidation Record. Service operations. Verify an existing acceptance; bind release to a specific immutable version; define release scope and effective period; set and change release status; run eligibility checks; withdraw, supersede or revalidate a release; preserve release history. Collaborations. Prerequisite: SVC-06 (acceptance), SVC-09 (version). Collaborating: SVC-08. Constrained by: SVC-16, SVC-17. Evidence from: SVC-15, SVC-19. Enforced interaction constraints. IC-08 (Release Separation). Authority boundary. Does not create versions (that is SVC-09); does not make the acceptance decision (that is SVC-06); does not derive or apply actionable forms. Release requires an existing acceptance and never manufactures one. Operating criticality. Governance-critical; fail-closed — no release without a bound, accepted version, and no automatic inheritance of release by a new version. Conformance condition. For every release, the immutable version released, its acceptance basis, scope, effective period, current status and predecessor or successor releases are recoverable, and no version is released without acceptance. SVC-11 · Dependency Service Service statement. Represents dependencies and dispositions objects and forms affected by change. Purpose. Prevent locally correct change from silently invalidating dependent knowledge. Realised capabilities. Accountable for C-CAP-07. Authoritative information objects. Dependency Record; Dependency Impact Record; Revalidation Requirement; Dependency Disposition Record; Suspension Recommendation. Service operations. Represent dependencies; determine impacted dependants; classify impact; disposition as revalidation, evolution, suspension or no-action; preserve impact decisions. Collaborations. Prerequisite: SVC-01 (resolution). Collaborating: SVC-09. Triggers: SVC-08 (suspension), SVC-09 (evolve dependants). Evidence to: SVC-18. Enforced interaction constraints. Participates in INV-15 (dependency disposition); raises IC-03 suspension triggers. Authority boundary. Does not execute change or transition; does not accept or release; does not itself apply forms. Operating criticality. Governance-critical; fail-closed — a changed object does not return to use with undispositioned dependants. Conformance condition. For every material change, affected dependants and their recorded disposition are recoverable before the changed object returns to operational use. Part V · Domain D Services SVC-12 · Operationalisation Service Service statement. Derives actionable forms from governed objects and controls their eligibility for use. Purpose. Convert represented knowledge into usable forms without severing warrant. Form-level release governed here is distinct from object-level release (SVC-10). Realised capabilities. Accountable for D-CAP-01. Authoritative information objects. Actionable Form; Derivation Record; Warrant Linkage; Form Release Record; Form Status. Service operations. Derive forms; distinguish provisional from released; link forms to source version, justification and acceptance; withdraw or replace forms on source change. Collaborations. Prerequisite: SVC-06, SVC-09. Collaborating: SVC-10 (release alignment). Constrained by: SVC-16. Evidence from: SVC-15. Enforced interaction constraints. IC-10 (Operationalisation Eligibility); IC-12 (Warrant Link Preservation). Authority boundary. Does not accept or release the underlying object; does not apply forms; does not permit provisional forms into use. Operating criticality. Operationally critical; fail-closed for release — a form is not made usable without a warrant linkage. Conformance condition. Every operationally eligible form traces to an accepted object version and carries an inspectable warrant linkage. SVC-13 · Application and Outcome Service Service statement. Governs material use of actionable forms and captures outcomes as governed evidence. Purpose. Keep use authorised, traceable and explainable, and close the loop back to the lifecycle. Realised capabilities. Accountable for D-CAP-02, D-CAP-03. Authoritative information objects. Application Record; Use Context Record; Eligibility Decision; Explanation Record; Application Participant Record; Outcome Record; Interpretation Record; Feedback Record; Materiality Assessment; Disposition Record; Lifecycle Trigger. Service operations. Verify eligibility before use; record context and participants; preserve input-to-result path; produce modality-appropriate explanation; capture outcomes; assess materiality; assign disposition; raise lifecycle triggers. Collaborations. Prerequisite: SVC-12. Collaborating: SVC-08. Constrained by: SVC-07 (governance status), SVC-16. Triggers: SVC-07, SVC-09, SVC-08. Evidence from: SVC-15. Enforced interaction constraints. IC-11 (Application Eligibility); IC-12 (Warrant Link Preservation). Authority boundary. Does not derive forms; does not accept or release; does not execute evolution or retirement, only trigger them. Operating criticality. Operationally critical; fail-closed for use — an ineligible object is not applied. Outcome capture is recoverable within a defined, visible period. Conformance condition. For each material application, what was used, why it was eligible, who participated, the result and a proportionate explanation are recoverable, and every material outcome has a recorded disposition. SVC-14 · Retirement and Preservation Service Service statement. Concludes operational use of an object while preserving identity, records and lineage. Purpose. Remove knowledge from active reliance without destroying institutional memory. Realised capabilities. Accountable for D-CAP-04. Authoritative information objects. Retirement Record; Historical Object Record; Preservation Record; Reactivation Request; Successor Link. Service operations. Record retirement reason and authority; remove object and forms from active eligibility; preserve the historical record; maintain successor links; support historical retrieval; route reactivation through evolution. Collaborations. Prerequisite: SVC-01. Collaborating: SVC-08. Constrained by: SVC-16. Evidence from: SVC-19. Triggers: SVC-09 (reactivation via evolution). Enforced interaction constraints. IC-04 (Reactivation through Evolution). Authority boundary. Does not delete governed history; does not accept; does not permit reactivation outside governed evolution. Operating criticality. Governance-critical — destructive deletion of governed history is prohibited. Conformance condition. A retired object cannot be used operationally, yet its identity, versions, warrant, governance history and lineage remain recoverable. Part VI · Domain E Services (Cross-Cutting) The five Domain E services preserve and evaluate the governed context surrounding substantive knowledge. None authors or alters substantive content, and none independently authorises a lifecycle transition. They are ordered here from the most foundational (provenance) to the most derived (temporal reconstruction). SVC-15 · Provenance and Traceability Service Service statement. Preserves origin, derivation, custody, attribution and end-to-end traceability across all objects, records, transitions and applications. Purpose. Make current states and historical change reconstructable. Realised capabilities. Accountable for E-CAP-01. Authoritative information objects. Provenance Record; Custody Record; Derivation Link; Attribution Link; Traceability Path; Provenance Gap Record. Service operations. Preserve origin and derivation; trace representations, changes, forms, applications and outcomes; carry provenance across modality hand-offs; identify provenance gaps explicitly. Collaborations. Prerequisite: SVC-01. Constrained by: SVC-16. Evidence to: all services. Enforced interaction constraints. IC-20 (Provenance Continuity). Authority boundary. Does not author or alter substantive content; does not authorise transitions; does not evaluate conformance. Operating criticality. Governance- and conformance-critical; fail-closed at hand-offs — a hand-off that cannot preserve provenance is not silently completed. Conformance condition. For a representative outcome, the path from source and creation through use and outcome is reconstructable, with any provenance gaps exposed. SVC-16 · Access and Integrity Service Service statement. Restricts access and material action by assigned permission while preserving the permission ≠ authority distinction, and protects record integrity. Purpose. Protect governed records and operations against unauthorised access, alteration or disclosure. Realised capabilities. Accountable for E-CAP-03. Authoritative information objects. Access Policy; Permission Assignment; Authority Assignment Reference; Disclosure Constraint; Integrity Status; Administrative Action Record. Service operations. Identify actors; assign and revoke permissions; enforce action permissions; protect integrity; enforce disclosure and use restrictions; record administrative action. Collaborations. Collaborating: SVC-07. Constrains: all services performing a material action. Evidence from: SVC-19. Enforced interaction constraints. IC-13 (Authority Is Not Permission); IC-14 (Least Necessary Alteration); IC-15 (Material Administrative Action); IC-16 (Automated Authority Boundary). Authority boundary. Does not make governance decisions (acceptance, stewardship, retirement); grants permission, never authority; does not select security technologies. Operating criticality. Governance-critical; fail-closed — an unauthorised material action is refused by default. Conformance condition. For every material action, the actor’s required permission and, where applicable, the separate valid authority decision are demonstrable. SVC-17 · Operating Condition and Exception Service Service statement. Determines and exposes whether required services, controls and evidence are operational, degraded, failed, pending or indeterminate, and governs the consequences. Purpose. Prevent absent evidence, failed controls or unavailable services from appearing as success. This responsibility is materially different from provenance or protection: it is the architecture’s fail-safe determinant, and it directly protects INV-24 (No Silent Success). Realised capabilities. Accountable for E-CAP-04. Authoritative information objects. Operating Condition Record; Degradation Record; Exception Record; Compensating Control Record; Recovery Record; Failure Disposition Record. Service operations. Distinguish pass, fail, pending and indeterminate; represent degradation; determine fail-open or fail-closed posture; raise and bound exceptions; preserve compensating controls; trigger suspension or correction. Collaborations. Collaborating: SVC-08. Constrains: SVC-08, SVC-07, SVC-04, SVC-10 (fail-posture on gates, reviews, evaluations and release). Triggers: SVC-08. Evidence to: SVC-18. Enforced interaction constraints. IC-19 (Exception Visibility); participates in IC-02 (fail-posture at gates). Authority boundary. Does not execute the corrective transition (that is SVC-08); does not define organisational risk acceptance. Operating criticality. Conformance- and governance-critical; its own degradation defaults to fail-closed. Conformance condition. When a condition cannot be evaluated or a service is degraded, the condition is recorded explicitly and the predefined consequence applied, rather than treated as satisfied. SVC-18 · Conformance and Audit Service Service statement. Determines and demonstrates whether required capabilities, invariants, gates, controls and constraints are satisfied. Purpose. Prevent compliance from resting on structural resemblance or self-assertion. Realised capabilities. Accountable for E-CAP-02. Authoritative information objects. Conformance Assessment; Invariant Test Result; Constraint Test Result; Assurance Finding; Non-Conformance Record; Exception Reference. Service operations. Inspect records and control evidence; test invariants and prohibited paths; reconcile evidence across services; record findings; distinguish conformance, variation, exception and non-conformance; recommend suspension or correction. Collaborations. Evidence from: all services. Triggers: SVC-08 (via suspension recommendation), SVC-17. Enforced interaction constraints. IC-17 (Read-Only Assurance Boundary); IC-18 (No Sole Self-Certification). Authority boundary. Does not alter the records it examines; does not authorise transitions; is never an operational prerequisite of an operation it audits; does not certify its own outputs without independent evidence. Operating criticality. Conformance-critical but not transaction-blocking — its unavailability renders operations unproven, not halted. Conformance condition. The architecture can produce independently generated evidence for every required capability and report unmet, indeterminate or violated conditions without modifying the evidence assessed. SVC-19 · Temporal Continuity Service Service statement. Owns the governed temporal contract of the architecture: the meaning, sequence and authenticity of governed records and states across time, including as-of reconstruction. Purpose. Maintain trust where events, records and effective conditions occur at different times. This is a distinct authoritative responsibility, not a timestamp utility: it owns effective dating, event sequencing, as-of reconstruction, retention and correction history, and it alone can answer “what did the governed record say, and hold true, as of a stated time.” Realised capabilities. Accountable for E-CAP-05. Authoritative information objects. Temporal Metadata Record; Effective Period; Event-Time Record; Custody History; Retention Condition; Correction History; Historical Reconstruction Result. Service operations. Preserve recorded, effective and event time as three distinct semantics; sequence transitions and decisions; maintain correction history; preserve authenticity across format and custody change; reconstruct governed state as of a specified time; enforce retention and disposition. Collaborations. Collaborating: SVC-09 (append-only correction). Evidence from: SVC-15; Evidence to: SVC-18. Enforced interaction constraints. IC-21 (Append-Only Correction, with SVC-09); IC-22 (Time Semantics Preservation). Authority boundary. Does not perform version mechanics (that is SVC-09); does not select storage technology; does not alter substantive content. It owns time semantics and reconstruction , not the records’ substantive content. Operating criticality. Governance-critical; recoverable with bounded manual control, but never by relying on overwritten records. Conformance condition. The object’s content, warrant, acceptance, governance and operational state can be reconstructed as of a specified historical point — using recorded, effective and event time — without relying on overwritten current records. Part VII · Interaction Governance This part is the centre of KF-3003 . It fixes how services interact so that the interaction constraints hold in execution. 2. Service Interaction Principles Only the accountable service may alter an information object it authoritatively maintains; others request change through a governed interaction. Only SVC-08 may alter recorded lifecycle state. No transition executes without a gate decision bound to it in the same operation. No object is released (SVC-10) without an existing acceptance recorded by SVC-06 and a version created by SVC-09. No actionable form is derived or applied without a preserved warrant linkage. No governed record is overwritten; corrections append or version. No service acquires authority by holding permission. No automated service is the final accountable authority where human authority is required. SVC-18 reads all services and alters none, and is never a prerequisite of the operation it audits. Every material inter-service action is attributable and carries provenance. When a required condition is unavailable or indeterminate, SVC-17 determines the fail-posture; the default is fail-closed for governance-critical operations. 3. Constraint Enforcement Matrix Every interaction constraint is enforced at a named service boundary. Constraint Enforcing boundary Enforcement mechanism IC-01 · Lifecycle State Authority SVC-08 sole authority to write lifecycle state IC-02 · Gate Enforcement SVC-08 (with SVC-17) gate decision bound to transition; fail-posture on indeterminacy IC-03 · Suspension Ownership SVC-08 owns suspension; SVC-07/11/18 supply reason IC-04 · Reactivation through Evolution SVC-14 → SVC-09 → SVC-08 reactivation routed through evolution and re-acceptance IC-05 · Identity Immutability SVC-01 write-once identifier IC-06 · Version Immutability SVC-09 immutable version records IC-07 · Branch and Consolidation Identity SVC-09 (with SVC-01) successor identity with lineage links IC-08 · Release Separation SVC-10 (with SVC-06, SVC-09) release record distinct from version, bound to acceptance IC-09 · Justification–Acceptance Separation SVC-05 and SVC-06 separate authoritative maintainers; boundary tested by SVC-18 IC-10 · Operationalisation Eligibility SVC-12 warrant linkage required before release IC-11 · Application Eligibility SVC-13 eligibility check recorded before use IC-12 · Warrant Link Preservation SVC-12, SVC-13 non-nullable warrant links IC-13 · Authority Is Not Permission SVC-16 (with SVC-06) permission and authority held as separate records IC-14 · Least Necessary Alteration SVC-16 authoritative-maintainer boundary enforced IC-15 · Material Administrative Action SVC-16 administrative action log IC-16 · Automated Authority Boundary SVC-06, SVC-16 final authority resolves to a human role IC-17 · Read-Only Assurance Boundary SVC-18 read-only access to examined records IC-18 · No Sole Self-Certification SVC-18 independent evidence required per judgement IC-19 · Exception Visibility SVC-17 exception persists until closed IC-20 · Provenance Continuity SVC-15 provenance carried, not regenerated, at hand-off IC-21 · Append-Only Correction SVC-09, SVC-19 corrections append IC-22 · Time Semantics Preservation SVC-19 recorded, effective and event time preserved 4. Prohibited Cross-Service Actions No service may accept on behalf of another; write another service’s authoritative records directly; change lifecycle state outside SVC-08; release a version without an SVC-06 acceptance and an SVC-09 version; treat a permission from SVC-16 as an authority; present an SVC-18 assessment as an authorisation; or complete a hand-off that SVC-15 cannot make traceable. Part VIII · Completeness 5. Capability-to-Service Crosswalk Each capability names exactly one accountable service. Capability Accountable service Supporting services A-CAP-01 SVC-01 SVC-15, SVC-16 A-CAP-02 SVC-02 SVC-01, SVC-15 A-CAP-03 SVC-01 SVC-02, SVC-05, SVC-08 B-CAP-01 SVC-03 SVC-15 B-CAP-02 SVC-04 SVC-17 B-CAP-03 SVC-05 SVC-03, SVC-04 B-CAP-04 SVC-05 SVC-06 C-CAP-01 SVC-06 SVC-05, SVC-16, SVC-08 C-CAP-02 SVC-07 SVC-16 C-CAP-03 SVC-07 SVC-08, SVC-17 C-CAP-04 SVC-09 SVC-01, SVC-19 C-CAP-05 SVC-10 SVC-06, SVC-09 C-CAP-06 SVC-09 SVC-11, SVC-08 C-CAP-07 SVC-11 SVC-01, SVC-09 C-CAP-08 SVC-08 SVC-06, SVC-16, SVC-17 D-CAP-01 SVC-12 SVC-06, SVC-09, SVC-10 D-CAP-02 SVC-13 SVC-07, SVC-16 D-CAP-03 SVC-13 SVC-15 D-CAP-04 SVC-14 SVC-08, SVC-19 E-CAP-01 SVC-15 SVC-01 E-CAP-02 SVC-18 all E-CAP-03 SVC-16 SVC-07 E-CAP-04 SVC-17 SVC-08 E-CAP-05 SVC-19 SVC-15, SVC-09 Every capability has exactly one accountable service; no capability is unassigned and no service is without a capability basis. 6. Coverage Test The service architecture is complete when: every capability names exactly one accountable service; every governed information object has exactly one authoritative-maintainer service; every interaction constraint is enforced at a named boundary (§3); no service holds authority beyond its capabilities; no prohibited cross-service action is structurally possible; and the conformance service is read-only and non-prerequisite. Part IX · Service Conformance 7. Service Conformance A service conforms when it realises its accountable capabilities; is the sole authoritative maintainer of its information objects; exposes its operations without technology dependence; enforces its assigned interaction constraints; performs no prohibited action; and can demonstrate its conformance condition. As in KF-3002 , conformance is systemic: a service is not conformant where an unmet collaboration prevents a constraint it must enforce. 8. Service Evidence Evidence includes authoritative-ownership maps; operation traces; constraint-enforcement tests; prohibited-path tests; attribution and provenance checks; and independent assurance from SVC-18. Physical consolidation of services is permitted only where the authoritative-ownership boundary and constraint enforcement remain inspectable. Part X · Relationship to Subsequent Documents KF-3004 defines the information objects and record classes named here and fixes their authoritative-maintainer assignments and the recorded/effective/event time semantics owned by SVC-19. KF-3005 defines the gate logic and lifecycle controls that SVC-08 and SVC-17 apply, including the transactional gate–transition binding and the release eligibility checks of SVC-10. KF-3008 defines the human authority and accountability model that SVC-06 and SVC-07 depend upon, kept distinct from the technical permission SVC-16 assigns. KF-3007 defines the tests and evidence for service and constraint conformance. KF-3009 preserves traceability from principle through capability, service, record and control. Closing Statement The Service Architecture converts the twenty-four capabilities into nineteen governed logical services and, more importantly, into a set of enforced boundaries. Its contribution is not that the capabilities are exposed, but that they cannot be exercised in a way that bypasses one another: version is not release, release is not acceptance, permission is not authority, and assurance never authorises what it audits. Every interaction constraint is enforced at a named boundary; every governed record has a single authoritative maintainer; and no service holds authority it was not given. That is what makes this an execution architecture for governed knowledge rather than a catalogue of components.

t: KF-3004 · Governed Information and Record Model
d: The Logical Information Architecture of the Knowledge Foundry
x: Purpose KF-3004 defines the logical information objects, record classes, relationships, identity rules and temporal semantics required by the Knowledge Foundry architecture. It establishes what governed information must exist; how it is identified; how information objects relate; which single logical service maintains each authoritative record; how substantive, epistemic, governance, operational and assurance information remain distinguishable; how current and historical states are reconstructed; and how correction, supersession and retention operate without silent mutation. KF-3004 does not prescribe database technology, table structure, file format, graph implementation, indexing strategy, API payload, physical partitioning, vendor platform or user-interface representation. It answers: What logical information must a conforming Knowledge Foundry implementation preserve? Every record family in this document resolves to exactly one authoritative maintaining service in the frozen KF-3003 nineteen-service catalogue. There is no dual authoritative ownership: where two services touch a concept, one holds the authoritative record and the other holds an adjacent, related or derived view (§7.1). Information Derivation Every principal information object must be traceable to a lifecycle or practice obligation; a KF-3001 invariant or constraint; a KF-3002 capability; a KF-3003 service responsibility; and a conformance or historical-reconstruction need. Part I · Information Architecture Foundations 1. Core Information Concepts 1.1 Operational Knowledge Object. The enduring governed subject whose identity persists across versions, representations, assessments, releases and applications. The object is not identical to a document, file, row, model instance, prompt, version, actionable form or application result; it may be represented through one or more of these. 1.2 Object Version. An immutable represented state of an object. It belongs to exactly one enduring identity, captures a bounded substantive state, cannot be silently overwritten, may have several representations, may be evaluated/justified/accepted/released, and does not automatically inherit acceptance or release from another version. 1.3 Representation. An inspectable expression of the substantive content of a version — textual, symbolic, graphical, structured, computational, parametric, multimodal or hybrid. Representation identity is distinct from object and version identity. 1.4 Governed Record. An attributable, temporally situated information object preserving evidence of an event, decision, assessment, relationship, condition, assignment, action, outcome or conformance finding. It does not necessarily contain substantive knowledge. 1.5 Reference. A governed relationship to an information object maintained authoritatively elsewhere, preserving enough to resolve its target, identify the target version or effective state, detect broken resolution and preserve historical meaning. 1.6 Information Projection. A derived, cached or indexed view of authoritative information. A projection is not authoritative; it identifies its source records, preserves refresh/effective-state information, cannot silently override the authoritative record, and may be regenerated where required. 2. Information Classes Five classes, physically co-locatable but logically distinguishable: Substantive (what the object expresses); Epistemic (why, how strongly and under what uncertainty it may be believed); Governance (who may rely on it and under what conditions); Operational (how knowledge was transformed, used and observed); Assurance and continuity (how integrity, provenance, temporal continuity and conformance are demonstrated). 3. Information Object Admission Test Admitted where it is required to discharge an upstream obligation; has a distinct architectural meaning; has an identifiable single authoritative maintainer; has stateable identity or relationship semantics; has definable temporal behaviour; its absence would prevent control, traceability or conformance; it is not merely an undocumented attribute of another object; and it does not duplicate an existing authoritative record. 4. Information Object Specification Each principal information object may be specified through: Definition; Architectural purpose; Information class; Authoritative maintaining service; Identity rule; Required properties; Principal relationships; Lifecycle or status; Temporal semantics; Integrity and mutation rule; Retention and disposition; Protected invariants; Conformance test. 4.1 Information Object Granularity and Record Categories KF-3004 identifies logical information obligations. A named information object may be implemented as an independently identified governed record, an immutable sub-record, an effective-dated status assertion, a governed relationship, a controlled property, or a non-authoritative projection. A named item requires independent record identity only where it has its own authority, effective period, correction history, provenance, retention obligation, lifecycle or conformance significance. KF-4000 determines physical normalisation while preserving these semantics — a record code is not a mandatory database table. Each named object carries one of six record categories , which sets the specification depth required: Category Required specification Core Record all thirteen fields of §4 Supporting Record definition; maintainer; identity rule; required properties; parent/related core record; temporal and mutation rule Projection source records; freshness rule; invalidation rule; non-authoritative status Relationship Record the §9.1 relationship-type specification Status Assertion controlled value set; the core record it qualifies; effective-dating rule Controlled Vocabulary permitted values and their governing service Core records in this document are OBJ-01, VER-01, ACC-01, TRN-01, REL-01, ACT-01, APP-01, RET-01, PRO-01, CNF-05. All others are supporting records, projections, status assertions or relationship records as marked. 5. Common Record Properties Every governed record must contain or resolve to: stable record identity; record class; related object identity; related version identity where applicable; creator or originating service; initiating actor; accountable authority where applicable; recorded time; event time where distinct; effective time or period where applicable; status; provenance; integrity status; access classification; supersession or correction relationship; retention condition; authoritative maintaining service. A governed reference suffices where resolution and historical meaning are preserved. 5.1 Material Information Activity “Material” is defined, so implementations neither record everything nor lose accountability. An activity is material where it can affect: identity; substantive content; epistemic standing; authority; acceptance; lifecycle state; release eligibility; dependency disposition; operational application; outcome interpretation; access or integrity; historical reconstruction; or conformance. The authoritative definition of materiality, and the assurance-class scale that grades the depth to which material obligations must be discharged, are fixed by KF-2003 · Materiality and Assurance ; KF-3005 or a domain governance profile may set additional thresholds within it. 5.2 Event-Native Conformance Evidence Conformance evidence is, wherever possible, emitted by the governed act, not authored separately from it. The record that a governed act produces is its conformance evidence: an Acceptance Record is the evidence of acceptance; a Transition Record is the audit event; an Evaluation Verdict is the test result; a provenance link is the evidence of derivation; a Supersession Link is the evidence of lineage. A distinct evidence artefact is created only where the act’s own record cannot carry the required proof. This rule prevents a second knowledge-management problem — the management of evidence that the knowledge was managed — and is enforced architecturally by KF-3001 IC-24 and realised in the transition pattern of KF-3005 §35. 6. Identity Layers Identifiers are not interchangeable, and none may be reused for a different governed entity. 7. Authoritative Maintenance Every information object class has one authoritative maintaining service, which creates or accepts the record, applies authorised change, preserves history, rejects unauthorised mutation, exposes current and historical state, records correction and supersession, and supplies assurance evidence. Other services may reference, annotate, request change, create supporting records or maintain projections — never overwrite the authoritative record. Maintenance responsibility does not confer human decision authority. 7.1 Adjacent Information Responsibilities There is no dual authoritative ownership. Where two services touch one concept, one holds the authoritative record and the other holds an adjacent, related or derived view. Enforced by IC-14 (Least Necessary Alteration). Concern Authoritative record Authoritative service Related / derived information Institutional authority / mandate / delegation AUT-01, AUT-02 SVC-06 Authority and Acceptance KF-3008 governs the authority model ; SVC-16 assigns the technical permissions through which authorised actions execute Technical permission ACS-02 SVC-16 Access and Integrity executes actions authorised under AUT-01 Effective period of a substantive record that record its own maintaining service SVC-19 governs the common temporal model, sequencing and reconstruction — not each record’s validity decision Version correction COR-01 SVC-09 Version and Lineage temporally reconstructed by SVC-19 (no separate “correction history” record) Version supersession SUP-01 SVC-09 Version and Lineage release supersession is a distinct assertion held by SVC-10 Release supersession REL-01/REL-02 SVC-10 Release references SUP-01 where a version supersession is involved Current custody PRO-03 SVC-15 Provenance historical custody sequence reconstructed by SVC-19 (no separate “custody history” record) Evaluation confidence EVA-02 SVC-04 Evaluation distinct from epistemic confidence Epistemic standing / confidence EPS-01 SVC-05 Justification distinct from evaluation confidence Operational exception EXC-01 SVC-17 Operating Condition governance exception GOV-01 is held by SVC-07; SVC-18 reads both Reactivation REA-01 SVC-14 Retirement and Preservation enters governed evolution through a Change Record (CHG-01, SVC-09) — there is no separate “reactivation proposal” record Revalidation is not a separately owned record: it appears as a disposition value in DEP-03 (dependency-driven) and as a condition on REL-01 (release-side). 7.2 Composite Decision Records A composite decision (for example a release, which relies on an accepted version, valid acceptance, applicable authority, standing governance, dependency disposition and operating condition) must reference the authoritative records on which it relied — their identity, applicable version or effective state and decision-time status — and must not reproduce their substantive content in a way that creates a competing source of truth. This rule is load-bearing for KF-3005 gate definitions. Part II · Relationship Architecture 8. Relationship Types Identity — VERSION_OF, REPRESENTS_VERSION, RECORD_CONCERNS_OBJECT. Derivation — DERIVED_FROM, TRANSFORMED_FROM, GENERATED_USING, CONSOLIDATED_FROM. Evidential — SUPPORTS, CHALLENGES, CONTEXTUALISES, EVALUATES, JUSTIFIES. Governance — ACCEPTS, STEWARDS, AUTHORIZES_RELIANCE_ON, RELEASES, SUSPENDS, RETIRES. Lifecycle — TRIGGERED_BY, EVALUATED_UNDER_GATE, TRANSITIONS_FROM, TRANSITIONS_TO, RETURNS_TO. Dependency — DEPENDS_ON, IMPLEMENTS, USES, CONSTRAINED_BY, INVALIDATED_BY_CHANGE_TO. Operational — DERIVES_FORM, APPLIES_FORM, PRODUCES_OUTCOME, EXPLAINED_BY, FEEDS_BACK_TO. Historical — PRECEDES, SUCCEEDS, SUPERSEDES, CORRECTS, BRANCHES_FROM, CONSOLIDATES, REACTIVATES. 9. Relationship Properties Every material relationship must identify: relationship identity; source information object ; target information object ; relationship type; asserting actor/service; recorded time; effective period where relevant; provenance; status; confidence or qualification where applicable; supersession or correction history. (Relationships may connect records, versions, forms or outcomes — not only Operational Knowledge Objects.) 9.1 Relationship-Type Specification Each load-bearing relationship is specified through: relationship code; definition; permitted source class; permitted target class; direction; cardinality; symmetry; transitivity; effective-time behaviour; qualification or confidence; authoritative asserting service; correction and withdrawal rule. The most load-bearing relationships: Relationship Source → Target Cardinality Sym. Trans. Asserting service VERSION_OF Version → Object many-to-one (exactly one target) no no SVC-09 REPRESENTS_VERSION Representation → Version many-to-one no no SVC-02 SUPPORTS Evidence → Claim/Version many-to-many, qualified no no SVC-03 CHALLENGES Evidence → Claim/Version many-to-many, qualified no no SVC-03 ACCEPTS Authority → Version many-to-one per decision no no SVC-06 RELEASES Release → Version one-to-one per release no no SVC-10 DEPENDS_ON Object/Form/App → Object/Form many-to-many, directional no no (explicit only) SVC-11 DERIVED_FROM Info object → source input(s) many-to-many no yes (preserving basis) SVC-15 APPLIES_FORM Application → Actionable Form many-to-one no no SVC-13 PRODUCES_OUTCOME Application → Outcome one-to-many no no SVC-13 SUPERSEDES Entity → prior Entity one-to-one per scope no yes (chain) service owning the superseded entity Remaining relationships are completed in a controlled relationship registry using the same template. SUPERSEDES is a shared relationship type : its assertion is maintained by the service responsible for the superseded entity (a superseded version by SVC-09, a superseded release by SVC-10, a superseded form by SVC-12). 10. Relationship Integrity Rules Every relationship resolves to valid source and target identities. A relationship must not imply authority beyond its defined semantics. A broken relationship is represented explicitly. Historical relationships are not deleted when superseded. Derived relationships preserve their basis. Symmetry and transitivity are not assumed unless the type defines them. Dependency direction is explicit. Relationship status and object status remain distinct. Relationship correction creates a new governed state or correction record. Part III · Temporal and Historical Architecture 11. Time Semantics Event time , recorded time , effective time , decision time and processing time may coincide but must not be treated as identical by default. SVC-19 (Temporal Continuity) governs the common temporal model, historical sequencing and reconstruction rules. Each authoritative maintaining service remains responsible for the effective period and temporal assertions of the records it maintains — SVC-06 for an Acceptance Record’s effective period, SVC-10 for a Release Record’s, SVC-07 for a Stewardship Assignment’s. SVC-19 owns temporal conventions, sequence integrity, reconstruction and migration history; it does not approve or maintain each substantive validity decision. 12. Effective Periods A record governing continuing conditions must support effective-from, effective-to, open-ended validity, scheduled future effect, retrospective recording, revocation, supersession, suspension and reactivation. A later recorded fact may have an earlier effective time , so reconstruction must not rely solely on record-creation order. 13. Historical Reconstruction The architecture must reconstruct, at a specified time: substantive representation; epistemic standing; acceptance and release status; steward and applicable authority; lifecycle state; known dependencies; actionable forms; operating and integrity condition; relevant exceptions; and historical application eligibility. Reconstruction must distinguish what the system knew then from what the system knows now about then . 14. Mutation, Correction and Supersession Governed records are not silently overwritten. Permitted patterns: append; new immutable version; status transition; explicit correction; supersession; revocation; expiration; historical annotation. A correction must preserve the original record, correction reason, correcting actor/service, correction time, corrected content or interpretation, and the relationship between original and corrected state. 15. Deletion and Disposition Logical deletion must not erase information required for identity continuity, accountability, provenance, historical reconstruction, legal/policy retention or conformance evidence. Disposition may include active/restricted retention, archival preservation, anonymisation, de-identification, cryptographic erasure of protected content, or deletion after retention expiry. The record of disposition remains governed where accountability requires it. 15.1 Current State and Event History Where both a current-state record and an event history exist: the event or transition record preserves the authoritative historical act; the current-state record represents the effective current state; both are updated or established within one governed operation; disagreement between them produces an indeterminate integrity condition; current state must be reconstructable from valid historical events; correction does not erase the original event. This applies to lifecycle state, release status, form status, epistemic standing, stewardship and operating condition. In each case the current-state record is an effective-dated assertion established transactionally with its event; it is not a free-standing mutable value. Part IV · Domain A — Identity and Representation Information Record Family A1 · Object Identity — maintained by SVC-01 · Object Registry OBJ-01 · Object Identity Record (Core Record). The authoritative record of an object’s enduring identity. Required properties: object identifier; object class; registration status; origin reference; registration time; registration decision; identity-resolution status; applicable predecessor or source relationship; current lifecycle-state projection or reference (authoritative state is LIF-01, SVC-08) . Principal relationships: HAS_VERSION; ORIGINATED_FROM; BRANCHES_FROM; CONSOLIDATES; HAS_STEWARD; HAS_LIFECYCLE_STATE. Mutation rule: object identifier immutable; classification and descriptive metadata may change through governed correction. Conformance test: every governed object resolves to exactly one enduring Object Identity Record, regardless of lifecycle state. Protects: INV-01, IC-05. OBJ-02 · Intake Record (Supporting). Submitted material, source, intake context, initiating actor, classification request, duplicate-search result, routing decision. OBJ-03 · Identity Resolution Decision (Supporting). Whether intake represents a new object, candidate version, branch candidate, consolidation candidate, duplicate or unresolved identity. Record Family A2 · Representation — maintained by SVC-02 · Representation REP-01 · Structured Representation (Supporting). Substantive content, semantic structure, constituent claims/elements, representation modality, limitations, object and version identity. REP-02 · Semantic Type Record (Controlled Vocabulary). Semantic classification applied to an object, representation, claim or relationship. REP-03 · Representation Limitation Record (Supporting). Known opacity, incompleteness, approximation, modality limitation, interpretation constraint, unsupported use. REP-04 · Object Relationship Record (Relationship Record). Governed semantic relationships among objects, versions or elements. Record Family A3 · Resolution and Discovery — maintained by SVC-01 · Object Registry (RES-02 is a projection) RES-01 · Resolution Result (Projection). Query/identifier supplied; target resolved; ambiguity; resolution basis; current or historical context; access filtering; retrieval time. RES-02 · Governed Context Package (Projection). A non-authoritative assembled view referencing identity, version, representation, epistemic standing, acceptance, release, lifecycle state, provenance, stewardship and restrictions. RES-03 · Retrieval Provenance Record (Supporting). Requested information; requester; source records accessed; projection/cache use; version returned; retrieval time. Part V · Domain B — Evidence and Justification Information Record Family B1 · Evidence — maintained by SVC-03 · Evidence EVD-01 · Evidence Record (Supporting). Evidence identifier; type; origin; creator/source; content or source reference; custody; availability; integrity status; effective period where applicable. EVD-02 · Evidence Relationship Record (Relationship Record). Relates evidence to claim, object, version, evaluation or justification; role: supports, challenges, limits, contextualises, corroborates. The “counter” quality belongs to this relationship role, not to the evidence object — the same evidence may support one claim and challenge another. EVD-03 · Material Counter-Evidence Assertion (Supporting). Exists only where a material challenge must be made visible in acceptance and review. It preserves INV-06 without implying that an item is intrinsically “counter-evidence.” Protects: INV-06. EVD-04 · Evidence Availability Status (Status Assertion). Available, restricted, unavailable, inaccessible, destroyed, unresolved, provenance-incomplete. Record Family B2 · Evaluation — maintained by SVC-04 · Evaluation EVA-01 · Evaluation Criteria Record (Supporting). Criterion; applicability; threshold; scoring/judgement method; effective period; exception rule. EVA-02 · Quality Assessment Record (Supporting). Object/evidence assessed; criteria applied; evaluator; inputs; findings; evaluation confidence (distinct from epistemic confidence — §7.1) ; limitations; assessment time. Includes an assessment-progression value: not assessed, pending, in progress, completed, reassessment required. EVA-03 · Evaluation Verdict Record (Status Assertion). Pass, fail, return, pending, indeterminate; never inferred solely from score. Protects: INV-24. EVA-04 · Evaluation Exception Record (Supporting). A permitted procedural deviation that does not convert an invariant violation into conformance. Record Family B3 · Justification and Epistemic Standing — maintained by SVC-05 · Justification JUS-01 · Justification Record (Supporting). Structured warrant referencing claims, evidence, counter-evidence assertions, evaluations, rationale, assumptions, unresolved challenges, confidence, limitations. Protects: INV-05, IC-09. JUS-02 · Assumption Record (Supporting). Statement; source/basis; scope; confidence; materiality; review condition. JUS-03 · Rationale Record (Supporting). The reasoning connecting evidence and assumptions to a conclusion. JUS-04 · Challenge Record (Supporting). A resolved or unresolved challenge to the warrant. EPS-01 · Epistemic Standing Record (Status Assertion). The current epistemic conclusion: unsupported, provisionally supported, supported, strongly supported, weakened, indeterminate. Independent of lifecycle, acceptance and release, and independent of assessment progression (held in EVA-02) and contestation (EPS-03) . Protects: INV-03, INV-07. EPS-02 · Epistemic Standing Change Record (Supporting). Prior standing; new standing; triggering evidence or assessment; responsible actor/service; recorded and effective time. EPS-03 · Contestation Status Record (Status Assertion). Not contested, contested, materially contested, resolved. An object may be supported and contested simultaneously; these are separate dimensions. Part VI · Domain C — Governance and Change Information Record Family C1 · Authority and Acceptance — maintained by SVC-06 · Authority and Acceptance AUT-01 · Authority Mandate Record (Supporting). Authority holder or accountable body; source; mandate; scope; effective period; delegation; constraints; revocation status. Part IX · Information Integrity Rules 16. Object and version integrity. One enduring identity per object; every version belongs to one object; version content immutable after establishment; new versions do not create new object identities; branching and consolidation create successor identities; release and acceptance do not create versions; retirement does not erase identity. 17. Record integrity. Every material event and decision (per §5.1) has a governed record; records are attributable; material records preserve applicable authority; corrections do not erase originals; record status is explicit; missing information is not represented as affirmative evidence; projections do not supersede authoritative records; records under assurance review cannot be silently altered; a composite decision references rather than copies the records it relied on (§7.2). 18. State separation. These remain distinct, none inferred solely from another unless KF-3005 defines a formal derivation rule: object lifecycle state; version status; representation status; epistemic standing; assessment progression; contestation; acceptance status; release status; actionable-form status; service operating condition; conformance status. 19. Authority and permission separation. A permission record (ACS-02, SVC-16) establishes that an actor/service may technically perform an action; an authority record (AUT-01, SVC-06) establishes that a human authority or accountable body may make a governed decision. Both may be required; neither substitutes for the other. 20. Provenance integrity. Every material information object preserves or resolves to origin, creator/source, derivation, custody, related object and version, material transformation and known gaps. Broken provenance is explicit. 21. Temporal integrity. Recorded time is never substituted for effective time; retrospective recording is identified; future-effective decisions are not treated as currently effective; expired decisions do not remain silently active; reconstruction preserves knowledge available at the target time; later correction is distinguishable from the earlier state; sequence ambiguity is represented as indeterminate where unresolved. Part X · Information Interaction Contracts 22. Record creation. A service may create an authoritative record only where KF-3003 assigns it maintenance responsibility. 23. Record reference. A referencing service preserves target identity, target version or effective state, relationship type, reference time and resolution status. 24. Change request. A service may request but not directly apply change to another service’s record. 25. Event publication. Material creation, change, suspension, withdrawal, correction and retirement events are made available to affected services without transferring authority or mutating receiving records. 26. Projection and caching. A projection identifies authoritative source, source version or effective state, creation time, freshness and invalidation conditions and access restrictions; a stale projection is never presented as current authoritative state. Part XI · Information Conformance 27. Information conformance. Every required object class is represented; every authoritative record has one maintaining service; identity semantics are preserved; required relationships are resolvable; current and historical states are distinguishable; correction and supersession preserve prior states; temporal semantics are explicit; protected information is access-controlled; missing or indeterminate information is visible; and information supports all required invariant and interaction-constraint tests. 28. Information conformance evidence. Logical information model; authoritative-maintainer matrix; identity tests; relationship-integrity tests; temporal-reconstruction tests; correction and supersession tests; version-immutability tests; state-separation tests; access and authority checks; provenance-path reconstruction; cross-service reconciliation; retention and disposition evidence. 29. Representative reconstruction test. The reconstruction must also reveal the responsible human authority, applicable steward, lifecycle transitions, dependencies, access and integrity condition, operating condition, known provenance gaps, relevant exceptions and conformance findings.
